groundedIn: Real code only (grep/ripgrep + backend/prisma/schema.prisma). Every claim cites a model name, service class, or file:line.
domainsCovered: Tenant-user identity (Agent — email/password/role/MFA/KYC/OAuth all on one model)
OAuth / social login (Google, Apple, Facebook, TikTok) + SocialAccount linking
Collaborator/partner invitation (CollaboratorInvite model — parallel to team)
Platform admin identity, auth, session, MFA, audit (AdminUser stack — fully parallel)
Rate limiting / login-attempt throttling (two separate implementations)
keyArchitecturalFacts: There is NO `User` model. `Agent` (table RAC_Agent, schema.prisma:306) IS the tenant user: it carries email, password (bcrypt), role, MFA (mfaSecret/mfaEnabled/mfaPendingSetup), KYC, OAuth provider fields, and onboarding state. `Workspace` (table RAC_Workspace, schema.prisma:119) is the tenant root.

Membership is implicit: an Agent belongs to exactly one Workspace via Agent.workspaceId (@@unique([workspaceId, email])). There is no join/membership table — role lives directly on Agent (role + displayRole).

Two completely separate auth universes exist: (1) the tenant `Agent` stack under backend/src/auth, and (2) the platform-operator `AdminUser` stack under backend/src/admin/auth. They duplicate password hashing, MFA/TOTP, session/refresh, login-attempt throttling, and audit logging with NO shared core.

Tenant sessions use opaque RefreshToken rows (PLAINTEXT token column) + JWT access tokens. Admin sessions use AdminSession rows (HASHED token_hash). Magic-link tokens are hashed (tokenHash). This hashing policy is inconsistent across token families.

canonicalEntities.name: Workspace
canonicalEntities.role: Tenant root / billing+branding+provider-settings container. Tenancy boundary for nearly every other model (workspaceId FK). customDomain @unique enables white-label reseller resolution.

canonicalEntities.name: Agent
canonicalEntities.role: THE tenant user identity. email+password(bcrypt)+role+MFA+KYC+OAuth provider fields. @@unique([workspaceId, email]). Owns refreshTokens, deviceTokens, passwordResetTokens, magicLinkTokens, socialAccounts.

canonicalEntities.name: RefreshToken
canonicalEntities.role: Tenant opaque refresh token. token @unique stored in PLAINTEXT (contrast AdminSession.token_hash / MagicLinkToken.tokenHash). revoked flag + expiresAt. Rotated atomically by AuthTokenService.

canonicalEntities.name: DeviceToken
canonicalEntities.role: Push/device token per platform (IOS/ANDROID/WEB) linked to Agent. Defined on schema but no service in target dirs writes it — see legacyOrDead.

canonicalEntities.name: PasswordResetToken
canonicalEntities.role: One-time password-reset token (token @unique, used flag, expiresAt) linked to Agent. Consumed by auth-service.password-verification.ts.

canonicalEntities.name: MagicLinkToken
canonicalEntities.role: Passwordless login token. Stores tokenHash @unique (HASHED via hashOpaqueToken sha256), email, redirectTo, usedAt. Optional agentId. Consumed by auth-service.magic-link.ts.

canonicalEntities.name: SocialAccount
canonicalEntities.role: OAuth provider link per Agent. @@unique([provider, providerUserId]) and @@unique([agentId, provider]). Stores access/refresh tokens + profileData. Written by auth-service.social-account.ts / OAuth resolver.

canonicalEntities.name: Invitation
canonicalEntities.role: TEAM invite: email+role+token(@unique)+expiresAt, @@unique([workspaceId, email]). Canonical home = TeamService. DUPLICATES CollaboratorInvite semantically.

canonicalEntities.name: CollaboratorInvite
canonicalEntities.role: COLLABORATOR invite: email+role+status(PENDING/REVOKED)+token+invitedBy+expiresAt. Canonical home = PartnershipsService. SECOND, divergent implementation of the same workspace-invite concept as Invitation.

canonicalEntities.name: ApiKey
canonicalEntities.role: Workspace-scoped API key. key @unique column DOCUMENTED as 'sk_live_...' but ApiKeysService stores a salted PBKDF2 hash there; validateKey scans up to 1000 rows (no index lookup possible on a salted hash).

canonicalEntities.name: Persona
canonicalEntities.role: AI persona (role/basePrompt/voiceId) that Agents can 'adopt' (Agent.personaId). Identity-adjacent: shapes an Agent's bot behavior, not an auth principal.

canonicalEntities.name: AdminUser
canonicalEntities.role: Platform-operator identity (separate DB table family, snake_case @map). passwordHash(bcrypt)+MFA+role(AdminRole)+status+allowedIps+lockout. Fully parallel to Agent for the admin console.

canonicalEntities.name: AdminSession
canonicalEntities.role: Admin refresh/session row. token_hash @unique (HASHED via sha256Hex) — contrast tenant RefreshToken plaintext. revokedAt + expiresAt. Rotated by AdminAuthService.refresh.

canonicalEntities.name: AdminPermission
canonicalEntities.role: Fine-grained admin RBAC (module+action+allowed). No tenant equivalent — Agent RBAC is a loose Json `permissions` array on the Agent model.

canonicalEntities.name: AdminAuditLog
canonicalEntities.role: Admin-side audit trail. Parallel to the tenant AuditLog model (schema.prisma:1374) + AuditService used by Team/ApiKeys.

canonicalEntities.name: AdminLoginAttempt
canonicalEntities.role: Admin login throttle ledger (email+ip+success). Parallel-but-different to the tenant RateLimitService (in-memory/Redis counter, not a table).

canonicalEntities.name: CookieConsent
canonicalEntities.role: Per-Agent cookie consent (necessary/analytics/marketing). Identity-adjacent compliance state.

canonicalEntities.name: DataDeletionRequest
canonicalEntities.role: Provider-initiated (OAuth) data-deletion request keyed by providerUserId. Identity/GDPR-adjacent.

services.name: AuthService
services.responsibility: Facade orchestrator. Delegates to standalone functions (register-login, oauth-entry, magic-link, whatsapp, password-verification) + AuthTokenService + AccountMfaService. Owns logout() and getMe().

services.name: AuthTokenService
services.responsibility: CANONICAL JWT + refresh-token issuance, atomic Serializable rotation with P2034 retry, replay-detection grace window, and access-token JTI blacklist (Redis key `jti:revoked:<jti>`).

services.name: AuthPasswordService
services.responsibility: ORPHAN. checkEmail/createAnonymous/register/login fully implemented but NEVER injected (0 non-spec refs, absent from auth.module.ts). Superseded by auth-service.register-login.ts standalone functions.

services.name: AccountMfaService
services.responsibility: Tenant TOTP MFA: createSetup/resumeSetup/verifyCode. Reuses encrypt/decryptAdminSecret from admin-crypto but REIMPLEMENTS the full TOTP engine (base32, generateTotp, verifyTotp).

services.name: GoogleAuthService
services.responsibility: Verify Google OAuth credential / ID token.

services.name: AppleAuthService
services.responsibility: Verify Apple identity token / authorization code.

services.name: FacebookAuthService
services.responsibility: Verify Facebook access token.

services.name: TikTokAuthService
services.responsibility: Exchange TikTok authorization code / access token.

services.name: AuthOAuthService
services.responsibility: OAuth login orchestration (provider-agnostic entry).

services.name: AuthOAuthResolverService
services.responsibility: Resolve/link an Agent + SocialAccount from a verified OAuth identity (find-or-create).

services.name: AuthVerificationService
services.responsibility: Email verification + resend flows.

services.name: AuthWhatsappPasswordService
services.responsibility: WhatsApp OTP send/verify passwordless login path.

services.name: AuthPartnerService
services.responsibility: Affiliate/partner invite-token handling during registration (affiliateInviteToken).

services.name: EmailService
services.responsibility: Transactional auth emails (reset, verify, team invite). Note: lives under auth/ but used by TeamService too.

services.name: RateLimitService
services.responsibility: Tenant-side login/abuse rate limiting (counter-based). Parallel to admin AdminLoginAttemptsService + route-class throttler guard.

services.name: UserNameDerivationService
services.responsibility: Derive a display name from email/OAuth profile.

services.name: DbInitErrorService
services.responsibility: Map raw DB-init errors to friendly ServiceUnavailable messages used across auth.

services.name: JwtAuthGuard
services.responsibility: Global tenant JWT guard. Verifies signature, honors @Public, checks Redis blacklist `jti:revoked:<jti>`, sets req.user = decoded JWT.

services.name: RolesGuard
services.responsibility: Role-based route gate using @Roles decorator metadata against req.user.role.

services.name: ApiKeysService
services.responsibility: Workspace API key list/create/rotate/delete/validate. PBKDF2 hash on store; validateKey does O(n) linear scan over up to 1000 keys.

services.name: TeamService
services.responsibility: Workspace member list/invite/accept/revoke/remove/update-role over Agent + Invitation. Enforces last-admin invariant (ensureLastAdmin).

services.name: WorkspaceService
services.responsibility: Workspace CRUD-lite + providerSettings merge (jitter, channels, business info/hours/policy, theme). Cache-wrapped getWorkspace.

services.name: PartnershipsService
services.responsibility: (adjacent) Collaborator list/invite/revoke/role over Agent + CollaboratorInvite — the SECOND team-invite implementation.

services.name: AdminAuthService
services.responsibility: (adjacent) Platform-admin login state machine, password change, MFA setup/verify, session refresh (rotate AdminSession), logout. Fully parallel to the tenant auth stack.

services.name: AdminMfaService
services.responsibility: (adjacent) Admin TOTP MFA. createSetup/resumeSetup/verifyCode + duplicate base32/generateTotp/verifyTotp engine identical to AccountMfaService.

services.name: AdminSessionFactory
services.responsibility: (adjacent) Mint admin scoped + full session JWTs and AdminSession rows. Parallel to AuthTokenService.

services.name: AdminLoginAttemptsService
services.responsibility: (adjacent) Admin login-attempt throttling backed by admin_login_attempts table. Parallel to tenant RateLimitService.

events: NO domain events / NestJS EventEmitter emits / BullMQ jobs are produced by any service in backend/src/auth, /api-keys, /team, /workspaces, or /admin/auth (grep for .emit/@OnEvent/Queue.add returned nothing in-cluster).
Side effects are fire-and-forget method calls, NOT events: AuthService.triggerWelcomeFlow -> WelcomeAndOnboardingEmailService.sendWelcomeEmail + scheduleOnboardingSequence (auth.service.ts:338).
Audit 'events' are synchronous DB writes via AuditService.log (tenant: ApiKeysService, TeamService) and AdminAuditService.append (admin) — append-only rows, not a message bus.

duplications.concept: Access-token logout blacklist uses a Redis key namespace that the guard never reads
duplications.canonicalChoice: Use AuthTokenService.revokeAccessToken (key `jti:revoked:<jti>`), the namespace JwtAuthGuard actually checks.
duplications.note: PROD BUG: a user who hits POST /auth/logout has their refresh tokens revoked, but their still-valid access token is written under `access-token-revoked:<jti>` which no code reads — the access JWT remains accepted until natural expiry. Two divergent key strings for one capability.

duplications.concept: Request -> workspaceId tenant resolver with DIVERGENT security semantics
implementations: backend/src/auth/workspace-access.ts:119 resolveWorkspaceId (SECURE: enforces requested===token.workspaceId, Forbidden on mismatch)
backend/src/kloel/guards/kloel-security.guard.ts:45 getWorkspaceId (reads params/body, IGNORES the JWT entirely)
backend/src/kloel/product-sub-resources/helpers/common.helpers.ts:20 getWorkspaceId (req.user?.workspaceId || req.workspaceId || '' — no cross-check, can yield empty string)
duplications.canonicalChoice: workspace-access.ts resolveWorkspaceId — the only variant that proves the caller owns the workspace.
duplications.note: Cross-tenant (IDOR) risk: any code path that selects the workspace via the kloel-security.guard or common.helpers variant trusts client-supplied workspaceId without checking it against the JWT. partnerships.controller already migrated to the secure resolver (explicit comment at line 45) — proof the team knows the others are unsafe but hasn't finished converging.

duplications.canonicalChoice: Pick ONE invite model. Invitation has the richer flow (email send + acceptInvite that provisions the Agent); CollaboratorInvite has the better schema (status enum, invitedBy, indexes).
duplications.note: Same capability (invite a person to a workspace by email+role+token+7-day-expiry) implemented twice with divergent behavior: Invitation sends an email and has a working accept->create-Agent path; CollaboratorInvite stores invitedBy + status but has NO observed email send and NO accept-creates-Agent path. A workspace could show two different pending-invite lists for the same person.

duplications.concept: Entire admin auth stack duplicates the tenant auth stack with no shared core
duplications.canonicalChoice: Extract a shared credential/MFA/session core; keep AdminUser vs Agent as the only divergence (principal table + RBAC granularity).
duplications.note: Password hashing (bcrypt@12), TOTP MFA, session rotation, login throttling, and audit logging are each implemented twice. Maintenance hazard: a security fix to one stack (e.g. the access-token-revocation key bug) does not propagate to the other. Justifiable as a blast-radius boundary, but the copy-paste is real.

duplications.concept: TOTP engine implemented identically in two MFA services
duplications.canonicalChoice: Hoist one TOTP util (e.g. backend/src/common/totp.ts); both MFA services import it. Secret encryption is ALREADY shared (admin-crypto), so only the codec/HOTP math needs extraction.
duplications.note: AccountMfaService already imports encrypt/decryptAdminSecret from admin-crypto, proving cross-module sharing is acceptable — yet the algorithmically identical TOTP code was copied rather than shared.

duplications.concept: Inconsistent token-at-rest policy across token families
implementations: ApiKey.key — PBKDF2 HASHED but column documented as plaintext 'sk_live_...' (schema.prisma:1649)
duplications.canonicalChoice: Standardize: store sha256(token) for all bearer tokens (matches AdminSession/MagicLink); query by hash. Keep PBKDF2 only for the API-key secret if a lookup index is added.
duplications.note: A DB read leak exposes live tenant refresh + password-reset tokens (plaintext) while admin/magic-link tokens stay safe. Same 'opaque bearer token' capability, three different at-rest treatments.

duplications.concept: ApiKey validation is an O(n) full-table scan
implementations: backend/src/api-keys/api-keys.service.ts:122 validateKey -> findMany(take:1000) then linear verifyStoredKey over every row
duplications.canonicalChoice: Store a deterministic lookup hash (sha256 of the raw key) in an indexed column for the WHERE clause, keep PBKDF2 only for the constant-time secret compare.
duplications.note: Because the stored value is a per-row salted PBKDF2 hash, no index lookup is possible, so every API request that authenticates by key scans up to 1000 keys and runs PBKDF2 (210k iters) per candidate. Scales poorly and is a DoS amplifier.

duplications.concept: Two bcrypt work-factor constants with the same value
duplications.canonicalChoice: Single exported constant in common/constants.ts referenced by both stacks.
duplications.note: Currently equal (12) so no behavior divergence today, but two sources of truth invite drift if one is bumped for a security upgrade and the other is forgotten.

duplications.concept: Stripe subscription -> workspaceId resolver copied across billing services
duplications.canonicalChoice: One shared resolver injected via the billing-*.helper port interfaces that already type it (billing-subscription-status.helper.ts:15).
duplications.note: Adjacent to the cluster but shares the resolveWorkspaceId name. Three private copies of the same subscription->tenant lookup; the port interface already exists, so the copies should collapse into the injected impl.

duplications.canonicalChoice: One shared sha256-hex helper in common/.
duplications.note: Both are createHash('sha256').digest('hex'); trivial but two homes for the identical primitive used by MagicLinkToken and AdminSession respectively.
